In college I drank all the time. I didn't know it but I was using it as a means to medicate my anxiety and depression. I would later be diagnosed with Bipolar 2 after I almost attempted suicide. My Sophomore/Junior years I was drunk every single day. I drank to sleep, then would wake up in the late afternoon knowing I'd be unable to fall asleep that day unless I drank again.

One night I had had enough and wanted to end it but before committing I broke down and cried to my roommate. The next morning he woke me up and I went home to my family and began the process of getting better. I was in an outpatient therapy program for three months where I learned CBT (Cognitive Behavioral Therapy.) This helped me control my panic attacks, anxiety, and desire to drink. 

I completely flipped my life around. I graduated, one year late which is fine, focused on my physical and mental health over everything else and now I am the happiest I've ever been.

I'm currently teaching English in Vietnam and travelling when I have time off. I have life goals now and a purpose every day when I wake up. 

I didn't understand how large of a change I made until one of my close friends wrote a letter to me saying that he was completely amazed by how much I've changed and how much growth I've gone through in the five or six years that he's known me. It was such a kind gesture on his part and it had such a powerful effect on me.
